A runtime system that dynamically selects and arranges enemies for a wave to hit a target difficulty curve, using the absolute 0-100 difficulty scorer delivered by AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K (Design a mechanism for calculating how hard an enemy is to survive).

## Context / provenance
Discovered during intake of AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K. The Producer chose the design-time scoring tool as the scope of that item and explicitly deferred the runtime auto-sequencer (round-2 Q4 answer (a)) so it can be tracked and scoped separately.

- Given a target difficulty for the next wave, choose enemy archetypes/groups (count, formation, mix) whose computed wave difficulty best matches the target.

# Screen shake and flash layers

## Goal
Add the two highest-impact juice layers — scene-camera shake and a brief
full-screen flash — as thin Phaser rendering helpers in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`,
tracked in a teardown registry and driven by the parameter model.

## User story
As a player, when my ship is destroyed the camera shakes hard and a bright cyan/
white flash frames the screen, so the moment feels weighty and unmistakable.

## Scope
- `applyShake(scene, params)` — calls `scene.cameras.main.shake(durationMs, intensity)` (full 2D); no-op when the layer toggle is off.
- `spawnDeathFlash(scene, params, registry)` — full-screen overlay (Rectangle/Graphics) at configured alpha/colour that fades to 0 over the configured duration, then destroys itself and splices out of the registry; no-op when disabled.
- Tests in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` using `src/test/gameHarness.ts` `bootScene` plus a camera spy.

## Constraints
- No behaviour change to gameplay; cosmetic only.
- Registry contract must mirror the existing `playerExplosions` pattern (`push` on spawn, `splice`/clear on completion and on SHUTDOWN).
- Flash must not block input or swallow pointer events (non-interactive).

## References
- Depends on task "Player-death juice parameter model and constants".
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC2, AC4, AC6); GDD §7.1 palette, §7.2 visual style.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Camera spy asserts `shake` is called exactly once with the configured intensity and duration for a `'respawn'` and a `'fatal'` call.
- [ ] The flash is created at the configured alpha/colour, tween duration matches the constant, and it is destroyed and removed from the registry on tween completion.
- [ ] Disabling the shake/flash toggles produces neither a shake call nor a flash object.
- [ ] Existing VFX tests remain green; `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- [ ] Covers parent AC2 — screen shake: a scene-camera shake is triggered on player destruction with configured intensity and duration.
data.title: Screen shake and flash layers

# Debris shards and shockwave ring

## Goal
Add two secondary juice layers that outlive the particle burst briefly — debris
shards and an expanding shockwave ring — each individually toggleable and
teardown-tracked.

## User story
As a player, the explosion reads as a layered event rather than a single puff:
shards fly outward and a ring expands past the ship before fading.

## Scope
- `spawnDeathDebris(scene, x, y, params, registry)` — N small filled shapes in the
  player colour, tweened outward with random directions and fade/shrink, destroyed
  and spliced on completion; seeded RNG option for deterministic tests.
- `spawnDeathShockwave(scene, x, y, params, registry)` — expanding stroked ring
  (Graphics) scaling to `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_RADIUS` over the configured
  duration, fading out, then destroyed and spliced.
- Both no-op when their `PLAYER_DEATH_ENABLE_*` toggle is off.
- Tests in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts`.

## Constraints
- Short-lived only; must not drop FPS or leak per-frame allocations.
- Reuse the existing seeded-PRNG pattern from `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` for
  deterministic tests.
- Colours centre on `SHIP_COLOR`.

## References
- Depends on task "Player-death juice parameter model and constants".
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC4, AC6).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Debris count and lifespan match the resolved params; shockwave radius/duration match the resolved params.
- [ ] Each spawned handle is added to the registry on creation and removed + destroyed on completion.
- [ ] Disabled toggles spawn nothing and leave the registry untouched.
- [ ] `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- [ ] Covers parent AC4 — extra juice layers (assumption-marked): at least two additional layers are configurable and individually toggleable.
data.title: Debris shards and shockwave ring

# Compose spawnPlayerDeathJuice entry point

## Goal
Provide the single shared entry point `spawnPlayerDeathJuice(scene, x, y, severity, options?)`
that composes every juice layer (camera shake, dedicated SFX, particle burst,
flash, debris, shockwave) so no scene has to know the layer set, and returns the
handles/registry so teardown can destroy everything.

## User story
As a developer, I call one function with a position and severity and the full
player-death effect plays; each layer is tunable/toggleable in one module and I
cannot accidentally play two sounds or two particle bursts.

## Scope
- `spawnPlayerDeathJuice(scene, x, y, severity, options?)` in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`:
  - resolves params via `resolveJuiceParams`;
  - plays `playPlayerDestructionSound()` exactly once;
  - calls `applyShake`, `spawnDeathFlash`, `spawnDeathDebris`, `spawnDeathShockwave`;
  - delegates particles to the existing `spawnExplosionParticles(scene, x, y, SHIP_COLOR, SHIP_SIZE, { patterns: resolvePatterns('player'), registry, ...severityOverrides })`;
  - returns a handle `{ params, registry }` (registry is the caller-owned array).
- `options` allows injecting the registry and a seed for deterministic tests.
- Tests in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` using the scene harness plus spies on the audio module and `spawnExplosionParticles`.

## Constraints
- The generic `playDestructionSound()` must NOT be called by this helper.
- Exactly one particle burst and exactly one dedicated sound per invocation.
- No gameplay state reads/writes; purely cosmetic.
- Keep the existing `_spawnPlayerExplosion` particle call as the particle source
  (the helper delegates) to avoid duplicate spawns when scenes are migrated.

## References
- Depends on the parameter model, dedicated SFX, shake/flash, and debris/shockwave tasks.
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC1, AC3, AC4, AC6).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A single call produces shake + exactly one dedicated sound call + particles + flash + debris + shockwave.
- [ ] `playDestructionSound()` is not called by the helper (spy assertion).
- [ ] Particles are spawned via `spawnExplosionParticles` with the `'player'` patterns and the caller's registry.
- [ ] The returned registry contains every juice-owned display object and is suitable for SHUTDOWN teardown.
- [ ] `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- [ ] Covers parent AC1 — shared player-death juice helper exists: a reusable helper composes the full effect and both player-death paths use it.
data.title: Compose spawnPlayerDeathJuice entry point

# Wire shared CombatScene.applyPlayerHit

## Goal
Route the shared combat base's player-hit VFX/respawn flow
(`CombatScene.applyPlayerHit`) through `spawnPlayerDeathJuice`, so the gym
formation scenes (`GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`, `GymMinerals`) get the full juice
without duplicating logic.

## User story
As a player training in the combat gyms, losing a ship has the same weighty
feedback as in the real run.

## Scope
- In `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` `applyPlayerHit(player)`, replace the
  direct `playDestructionSound()` + `_spawnPlayerExplosion()` calls with
  `spawnPlayerDeathJuice(this, player.x, player.y, 'respawn', { registry })`,
  keeping the scale-pulse tween, `player.respawnInPlace()` and
  `_startInvulnerability()` behaviour byte-for-byte equivalent.
- Ensure the particle burst is not spawned twice (the helper owns particles;
  `_spawnPlayerExplosion` is either re-pointed at the helper or made a thin
  delegate that does not double-spawn).
- Register a juice registry (`playerDeathEffects`) on the base and clear it in
  the existing SHUTDOWN teardown paths.

## Constraints
- No change to hit detection, lives, score, shield absorption, respawn position,
  invulnerability duration or blink timing.
- Gym scenes must not regress their existing tests.

## References
- Depends on "Compose spawnPlayerDeathJuice entry point".
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC1, AC3, AC5, AC6); `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `CombatScene.applyPlayerHit` calls the juice helper with `'respawn'` severity and spawns exactly one particle burst and exactly one dedicated sound.
- [ ] The scale-pulse tween, `respawnInPlace()` and `_startInvulnerability()` still run in the same order.
- [ ] SHUTDOWN clears the juice registry for the formation scenes (no leak across stop/restart).
- [ ] Existing combat/gym tests still pass; `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
data.title: Wire shared CombatScene.applyPlayerHit

# Wire PlayScene lose-life path

## Goal
Route the real-run player death (`PlayScene._loseLife`) through
`spawnPlayerDeathJuice`, using severity `'fatal'` for a run-ending death (final
life/game over) and `'respawn'` otherwise, while leaving the wave-timeout
penalty and shield-absorb paths unchanged.

## User story
As a player, losing my final life feels heavier than a mid-run respawn, and a
life lost in the real run has both the shake, the dedicated boom and the
explosion.

## Scope
- In `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_loseLife(explodeShip)`:
  - when `explodeShip` is true, call `spawnPlayerDeathJuice(this, player.x, player.y, severity, { registry })`
    with `severity = gameState.lives <= 0 ? 'fatal' : 'respawn'`;
  - remove the direct `playDestructionSound()` and `_spawnPlayerExplosion()` calls
    on that path (no double audio/particles);
  - when `explodeShip` is false (wave-timeout penalty, `_timeoutWave()`), keep the
    existing lighter audio behaviour and spawn no shake/flash/debris `[ASSUMPTION]`.
- Leave `tryAbsorbPlayerHit`'s shield-absorb `playDestructionSound()` untouched.
- Add/clear a `playerDeathEffects` registry in `_teardown()`.

## Constraints
- Respawn position, invulnerability duration, blink, lives/score accounting and
  shield absorption are unchanged; no hit-detection changes.
- Event ordering: VFX spawn before the game-over scene transition so `'fatal'`
  juice fires even though `_finishRun` starts `GameOverScene`.

## References
- Depends on "Compose spawnPlayerDeathJuice entry point".
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC1, AC3, AC5, AC6); AH-0MU3VQ0JR009CSIN (respawn in place).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `'fatal'` severity is chosen when `gameState.lives <= 0`, `'respawn'` otherwise, verified by a test.
- [ ] On the destroy path exactly one dedicated sound plays and the generic `playDestructionSound()` is not called; exactly one particle burst spawns.
- [ ] `_loseLife(false)` (wave timeout) spawns no shake/flash/debris.
- [ ] Shield absorb still plays the generic cue; lives/score/respawn/invuln unchanged.
- [ ] `_teardown()` clears the juice registry; `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
data.title: Wire PlayScene lose-life path

## Goal
Route the third, independently-implemented player-hit path —
`GymPowerUpsCombat._hitPlayer()` — through `spawnPlayerDeathJuice`, closing the
gap left by the intake brief which listed only two death paths.

## User story
As a player testing power-ups in the combat gym, losing a ship has the same
weighty feedback as in the real run and the formation gyms.

- In `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` `_hitPlayer()`, replace the local
  `playDestructionSound()` + inline `spawnExplosionParticles(...)` + scale-pulse

  preserving `playerHitCount`, the scale pulse, `respawnInPlace()` and
  `_startInvulnerability()`.

- P6 phase pass-through and P3 shield absorb ordering must remain: P6 → no hit;

# Cross-path regression and teardown sweep

## Goal
Prove the juice is wired consistently across **all** player-hit paths, that the
dedicated sound replaces the generic cue on those paths, and that no scene
leaks juice-owned objects across a stop/restart.

## User story
As a developer, I can trust that every player-death path gets the same juice
and that no display object survives a scene restart.

## Scope
- Integration tests covering, for each path:
  - the real run (`PlayScene._loseLife`, fatal + respawn),
  - the shared gym base (`CombatScene.applyPlayerHit` via `GymFormationScene`),
  - `GymPowerUpsCombat._hitPlayer()`;
  asserting: camera shake fired once with configured params, dedicated sound
  called exactly once, generic `playDestructionSound()` never called on the
  player path, particle burst spawned once, and every juice handle registered.
- Teardown tests: SHUTDOWN clears `playerDeathEffects` in `PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat`; a stop→restart produces no
  duplicate/stale display objects.
- Negative-path tests: shield absorb still uses the generic cue; wave-timeout
  `_loseLife(false)` triggers no shake/flash.

## Constraints
- Use the existing `src/test/gameHarness.ts` scene boot harness and spies;
  avoid brittle frame-timing assertions (drive tweens via captured
  `onComplete` callbacks like `src/vfx/bulletImpact.test.ts`).
- Update any existing assertions that assumed the old single-burst/single-sound
  player-hit behaviour rather than deleting coverage.

## References
- Depends on all three wiring tasks.
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC7, AC9).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each of the three player-hit paths has an integration test asserting shake-once, dedicated-sound-once, no generic sound, and one particle burst.
- [ ] Teardown tests assert the juice registry is emptied on SHUTDOWN for all three scenes and that stop→restart leaves no stale objects.
- [ ] A test asserts `_loseLife(false)` (wave timeout) triggers no shake/flash and that shield absorb keeps the generic cue.
- [ ] The full suite (`npm test`) and `npm run typecheck` pass, with no coverage removed.
- [ ] Covers parent AC6 — teardown / no leaks: all juice-owned GameObjects (flash) are tracked and destroyed on shutdown, no leaks.
- [ ] Covers parent AC7 — testing/validation: unit tests cover shake fired with configured params plus sound, flash, debris, severity and teardown.
- [ ] Covers parent AC9 — full project test suite must pass with the new changes, plus typecheck.
data.title: Cross-path regression and teardown sweep

# Documentation: GDD sections and code comments

## Goal
Document the new player-death juice and its tunables so designers and players
can reason about the effect, and so future work does not have to reverse-engineer
the constants.

## User story
As a developer/designer, the GDD explains every juice layer, the severity model
and where the tunables live; the code comments make each constant's purpose
obvious.

## Scope
- Update `docs/Game Design Document.md`:
  - §7.2 Visual Style — add a "Player-death juice" sub-bullet describing the
    composed effect (camera shake, dedicated SFX, particle burst, flash, debris,
    shockwave), severity scaling, per-layer toggles and the shared helper module.
  - §7.3 Audio Direction — add the dedicated player-destruction cue to the SFX
    Event Catalog ("Player hit (life lost)") and to the Player Audio Character
    table (wave/contour, volume) and note it replaces the generic enemy cue on
    player-death paths.
- Code comments/JSDoc on new exported constants and helpers in
  `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` and `src/audio/effects.ts`.
- Update `README.md` only if it documents audio/VFX behaviour.

## Constraints
- Match the existing GDD tone and table formatting; no invented requirements.
- Do not restructure unrelated GDD sections.

## References
- Depends on "Compose spawnPlayerDeathJuice entry point" (finalise after the
  wiring tasks so the documented paths are accurate).
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC8).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] GDD §7.2 documents the layered player-death juice, severity scaling and per-layer toggles, naming the helper module.
- [ ] GDD §7.3 lists the dedicated player-destruction cue with synthesis character and volume, and notes it replaces the generic cue on player-death paths.

## Problem statement

The Diver (E2) documentation still describes the dive as a **vertical drop with x locked at the formation slot**, but the implemented behaviour (AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX, "Diver should rotate to face the player and dive towards them") is a **diagonal parabolic dive** toward the snapshotted player position.

discovered-from:AH-0MUAYB6KL005A09Q

## Locations

- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1 (catalog) — "Vertical dive toward player (x locked at formation slot)".
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §7.3 (live aim tracking) — "Dives are x-locked at the formation slot."
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.2 (E2 Diver) — "Dives straight down toward the player (x locked at its formation slot — a vertical trajectory)".

## Expected behaviour

Docs describe the actual diagonal dive (both x and y follow the quadratic bezier from the formation slot to the player position snapshotted at dive start), and cross-reference the superseding behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** — The three locations above describe the diagonal dive and no longer state that x is locked.
- [ ] **AC2** — The docs mention the dive target is snapshotted at dive start (mid-dive aim changes do not alter the in-flight arc).
- [ ] **AC3** — Full project test suite must pass (docs-only change; this is a guard).

data.description:
Saving ship (or enemy) config from the gym overwrites `src/data/ship-config.csv` with only the header row + data row, dropping the `#` comment block that documents every column, enum values, and how to add entries.

**Why it matters:** the committed CSVs are documented as the "single, human-editable source of truth" (README "Configuration (CSV)"). After the first gym save, the human-readable column documentation is lost, making the file harder to hand-edit.

**Reproduction:** open the Player gym, change any value, click Save. Inspect `src/data/ship-config.csv` — the leading `#` comment lines are gone (see the `M src/data/ship-config.csv` diff on the working tree).

**Suggested approach:** have the dev-server plugin preserve the original comment prefix when rewriting the file, or move the column documentation out of the CSV (e.g. README/schema) so it is not destroyed by writes.

Discovered-from:AH-0MUESFKCD004SI1V

# ship producer-review gate remediation hint uses wrong `wl` flag casing

## Problem statement

The ship producer-review gate (exit 9) prints a remediation command that fails:

```
wl update <id> --needsProducerReview false --json
# -> error: unknown option '--needsProducerReview'
```

The `wl` CLI expects kebab-case `--needs-producer-review`. (The release audit runner emits the correct kebab-case form; only the human-facing remediation hint is wrong.)

## Impact

An operator/agent following the printed remediation verbatim cannot clear the producer-review flag, blocking an otherwise-green release.

## Location

Ship skill: `scripts/check-audit-gate.js` / `scripts/check-final-validation.js` producer-review remediation builders (`buildProducerReviewRemediationCommand`) — agent-infrastructure (`.pi/`/`skill/`), so reported here per the repository-boundary rule rather than edited inline.

## Suggested fix

Emit `--needs-producer-review false` (matching `wl update --help`).

## References

- Observed during release v0.1.5 (PR https://github.com/SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell/pull/5)
- discovered-from:AH-0MUFE1N36007X48T
data.title: ship producer-review gate remediation hint uses wrong wl flag casing

# Add Pages deploy trigger regression test

## Summary

Test-first verifier feature for *GitHub Pages deploy rejects release tags (environment policy allows only dev)* (`AH-0MUFGUR9C003XD77`). Adds an automated regression test that pins the **tag-only trigger contract** of `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`, so a future workflow edit cannot silently start deploying on branch pushes or pull requests.

## User story

As a future maintainer, I want an automated test that fails if the Pages deploy workflow starts triggering on non-tag events, so the tag-only release contract is protected without manual YAML review.

## Context

- Parent acceptance criterion **AC4** requires that `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` still triggers only on `v*` tag pushes, and that non-tag events (push to `main`/`dev`, pull requests) do not deploy.
- The workflow currently declares `on.push.tags: ['v*']` and a `deploy` job targeting environment `github-pages`.
- This item is created and completed **before** the environment-policy implementation items (test-first ordering).

## Scope

In scope:

- A hermetic vitest test that reads `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` from the repository root and asserts its trigger shape.

Out of scope:

- Changing the workflow (no change is expected for this fix).
- Calling the live GitHub API.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` still triggers only on `v*` tag pushes; non-tag events (push to `main`/`dev`, pull requests) do not deploy.
- The test asserts the only trigger is `push` with `tags: ['v*']` — no `branches`, no `pull_request`, and no `workflow_dispatch`.
- The test asserts the workflow contains a `deploy` job targeting the `github-pages` environment and a `build` job the deploy needs.
- The test is hermetic (reads only the checked-out workflow file) and runs as part of `npm test` with no new runtime dependency (`npm run build` and `npm test` both pass).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a vitest test (e.g. `scripts/deploy-pages-workflow.test.ts`, or co-located under `src/` if `scripts/` has no test wiring) that reads the workflow file using `node:fs` relative to the repo root.
- Parse the workflow text with focused assertions (regex/string checks or `yaml` if already available transitively); avoid adding a production dependency for a single test.
- Assert: `push.tags` is exactly `['v*']`; no `push.branches`; no `pull_request` / `workflow_dispatch` trigger keys; `jobs.deploy.environment.name == 'github-pages'`.
- Confirm the test is picked up by the existing `vitest.config.ts` include globs; adjust the include pattern only if the file lives outside the current test roots.

## Deliverables

- New automated trigger-contract test.
- `npm test` green including the new test.

## Dependencies

None.

## Key Files

- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` — The workflow whose trigger contract is asserted (no change expected).
- `vitest.config.ts` — Test include globs; may need to cover the new test location.
- `scripts/deploy-pages-workflow.test.ts` — New hermetic regression test.
data.title: Add Pages deploy trigger regression test

# Apply tag policy and verify deploy

## Summary

Applies the `tag:v*` deployment policy to the live `github-pages` environment using the setup script, then verifies the release Pages deploy end to end (policy present, `deploy` job succeeds, Pages URL serves the game).

## User story

As a release runner, I want pushing a `v*` release tag to deploy to GitHub Pages without environment-protection rejection, so that the release PR's checks pass and the ship wrapper merges the PR automatically; and as a player, I want every release published automatically at the project Pages URL.

## Context

- Parent acceptance criteria **AC1** (tag policy present) and **AC3** (deploy succeeds end to end) are verified by this item.
- Evidence of the current failure: workflow run `35993333739` (`event: push`, `headBranch: v0.1.5`) — `build` succeeded, `deploy` failed with zero steps due to environment protection.
- The active `gh` token has `repo` scope and the repository reports `admin: true`, so the script can apply the policy directly; if the token lacks admin the operator applies it manually and this item records the exact command.

## Scope

In scope:

# Intake Brief — Add globalWaveIndex accessor to WaveManager

- **Type:** task
- **Priority:** medium
- **Parent:** AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123

## Summary

Add a public accessor to `WaveManager` that returns the cumulative global wave index across the campaign, required by the new `AsteroidSpawner` to key escalation.

## Context

The asteroid spawner needs to know the cumulative wave count (across all levels) to drive the size-weight escalation. `WaveManager` currently tracks `_levelIndex` and `_waveIndex` but does not expose the sum.

## Implementation

1. Add a `globalWaveIndex` getter to `WaveManager` that returns the total regular waves before the current wave = sum of waves in levels 0..levelIndex-1 + waveIndex.
2. Update `beginGame()` and `reset()` to ensure the counter starts at 0.
3. The counter is implicit (derived from level/wave indices), so no extra state needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `globalWaveIndex` returns 0 for Level 1 Wave 1 after `beginGame()`.
2. `globalWaveIndex` returns the correct cumulative wave index after `onEnemyDestroyed()` advances through waves and levels.
3. For the shipped 5-level campaign (2+3+3+3+2=13 waves), the final regular wave has `globalWaveIndex` of 12.
4. `globalWaveIndex` returns 0 or -1 (never rises) when no regular wave is active (before `beginGame()`, during boss encounter).
5. Unit tests cover the accessor across wave/level transitions and boss state.

## Key Files

- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — add `globalWaveIndex` getter
- `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts` — add tests for the accessor

## Dependencies

- None (standalone change)

# Implement — AsteroidSpawner (pure planner)

- **Type:** task
- **Priority:** medium
- **Parent:** AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123

## Summary

Create `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` — a pure (no Phaser dependency) planner module that computes when and where asteroids should spawn based on the global wave index.

## Module Structure

### Exported types

```typescript
export interface SpawnEvent {
  sizeTier: 'large' | 'medium';
  x: number;
  y: number;
  vx: number;
  vy: number;
}
```

### Exported function

```typescript
export function computeSpawns(
  globalWaveIndex: number,
  gameWidth: number,
  gameHeight: number,
  waveTimeLimit: number,
  rng: () => number,
): SpawnEvent[];
```

## Algorithm (per spec)

### 1. Per-wave count

Start at 2. Every time the large weight reaches the reset threshold, double: `2 → 4 → 8 → …`.

### 2. Size weighting

- Medium weight fixed at 80.
- Large weight starts at 20 and increases by +20 per wave.
- When large weight reaches 2 × medium (160), reset to 80:20 and double the count.

Formula: `largeWeight = min(20 + 20 * (globalWaveIndex % wavesPerReset), 160)` where `wavesPerReset` depends on when the reset threshold is hit.

### 3. Spawn timing

- Divide the wave into N equal segments (N = count).
- Anchor for asteroid i is `i / N`.
- Apply ±5% jitter, clamped to [0, 0.95].
- First asteroid constrained to first 10% of wave.
- Times must be ordered and non-duplicated.

### 4. Offscreen edge + velocity

- Choose random edge uniformly (top/bottom/left/right).
- Place asteroid at random point along that edge, offset outward by `halfSize + margin` so fully outside viewport.
- Give inward-directed velocity: perpendicular to spawn edge with ±30° spread, at the tier's canonical speed.
- The inward component must dominate so it enters the playfield promptly.

### 5. Tuning constants (exported for easy retuning)

```typescript
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_BASE_COUNT = 2;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_BASE_LARGE_WEIGHT = 20;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_MEDIUM_WEIGHT = 80;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_LARGE_WEIGHT_INCREMENT = 20;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_LARGE_WEIGHT_RESET = 160;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_JITTER_FRACTION = 0.05;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_MAX_JITTER_FRACTION = 0.95;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_FIRST_ASTEROID_MAX_FRACTION = 0.10;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_INWARD_ANGULAR_SPREAD = Math.PI / 6; // ±30°
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_OUTWARD_MARGIN = 10; // px beyond half-size
```

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `computeSpawns` returns exactly `count` events for any `globalWaveIndex >= 0`.
2. Spawn count starts at 2 for `globalWaveIndex` 0–6, doubles at 7 (4), consistent with weight escalation.
3. Large weight increases by +20 per wave; resets when it reaches 2× medium weight (160).
4. First spawn time fraction is ≤ 0.10; subsequent times are spread across the wave with jitter.
5. All spawn positions are fully offscreen (distance from viewport ≥ asteroid half-size + margin).
6. All velocity vectors have inward components (toward the viewport centre).
7. Output is deterministic for a given `globalWaveIndex`, dimensions, and RNG sequence.
8. No Phaser runtime dependencies — pure TypeScript functions only.

## Key Files

- `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` — new module
data.title: Implement — AsteroidSpawner (pure planner)

# Test — AsteroidSpawner deterministic unit tests

- **Type:** task
- **Priority:** medium
- **Parent:** AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123

## Summary

Create `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.test.ts` with deterministic unit tests for `computeSpawns`.

## Test Scenarios

### Count progression
1. Baseline count is 2 for `globalWaveIndex` 0.
2. Count is 2 through waves 0–6 (large weight 20→140, below 160 reset).
3. Count doubles to 4 at wave 7 (large weight reaches 160, reset triggers double).
4. Verify count progression logic matches the spec (2→4→8).

### Weight escalation and reset
5. Large weight starts at 20 for `globalWaveIndex` 0.
6. Large weight increases by +20 per wave (20, 40, 60, ..., 160).
7. Weight resets to 20 when it reaches 160 (2 × medium weight 80).
8. After reset, count doubles (2→4).

### Spawn timing
9. First asteroid spawn time fraction ≤ 0.10.
10. Spawn times are ordered (non-decreasing).
11. Spawn times include jitter but remain within [0, 0.95].
12. For count=4, spawns are spread across the wave (roughly 0.05, 0.30, 0.55, 0.80).

### Offscreen positions
13. All spawn positions are fully outside the viewport (x < 0 or x > width or y < 0 or y > height).
14. Minimum distance from viewport edge ≥ halfSize + margin.

### Inward velocity
15. For top-edge spawns, vy > 0.
16. For bottom-edge spawns, vy < 0.
17. For left-edge spawns, vx > 0.
18. For right-edge spawns, vx < 0.
19. Angular spread is ≤ ±30° from perpendicular.

### Determinism
20. Same `globalWaveIndex`, dimensions, and RNG sequence produces identical output.

## Key Files

- `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.test.ts` — new test file
